newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: FOREIGN SALES WEAKEN SLOVAK CROWN IN NERVOUS TRADE.
newsitem.headline: FOREIGN SALES WEAKEN SLOVAK CROWN IN NERVOUS TRADE.

text.p: The Slovak crown weakened by some 45 basis points in nervous afternoon activity, pushed down by massive sales by foreign banks, dealers said on Thursday.

They estimated that some $100 million had left the country during the day amid a similar withdrawals in the Czech Republic where the crown fell sharply early forcing the central bank to intervene on the market.
Traders say foreign players are trading the Czech and Slovak crowns together, effectively implying a depreciation trend on both currencies.
"We think the Slovak crown may further weaken today, and could even to test a -1.0 percent levels versus its (mark/dollar) basket midpoint," said one Bratislava-based dealer from a foreign bank.
At 1100 GMT the crown was trading at around -0.75 percent against the basket parity.

The NBS on Wednesday fixed the crown at 32.990 to the dollar and at 19.542 to the mark, implying a deviation against the basket midpoint of -0.25 percent. The crown was trading at some -0.61 percent versus its partity at the time of the fixing calculation.

The CNB on Thursday morning twice directly intervened on the market to support the crown and helped it stabilise at less than four percent below parity, after it had touched levels at around minus 5.0 percent.
"On the other hand, the National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) sent a signal to the market through its fixing that it does not want the crown to fall too much," the dealer said.
